content:
{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "PFS primary endpoint lacks explicit definition of 'progression' for non-measurable disease",
      "quote": "Progression will be based on an independent radiologic assessment of disease response per Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors version 1.1 (RECIST v1.1).",
      "page": 38,
      "section": "2.1.2 Primary Endpoints",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The protocol does not specify how progression is determined for subjects with non-measurable disease only, which is common in NSCLC. RECIST v1.1 has specific rules for non-target lesions, but the protocol should explicitly state that progression can be based on non-target lesions or new lesions to avoid ambiguity and potential misclassification.",
      "fix": "Add a sentence clarifying that progression includes unequivocal progression of non-target lesions or appearance of new lesions per RECIST v1.1."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inclusion criterion 105 requires both platinum-based doublet and checkpoint inhibitor, which may be overly restrictive and cause enrollment delays",
      "quote": "Prior treatment must include a platinum-based doublet chemotherapy and checkpoint inhibitor for advanced or metastatic disease, either given as one line of therapy or as individual lines of therapy unless the subject has a medical contraindication to one of the required therapies.",
      "page": 58,
      "section": "5.1 Inclusion Criteria",
      "category": "amendment_risk",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Requiring both a platinum-based doublet and a checkpoint inhibitor as prior therapy may exclude patients who received only one due to rapid progression or other reasons, and the exception for medical contraindication is subjective. This could slow enrollment and lead to amendments if the population is not as broad as intended.",
      "fix": "Consider allowing prior therapy with either a platinum-based doublet or a checkpoint inhibitor, or specify objective criteria for medical contraindication to reduce ambiguity."
    },
    {
      "title": "PRO endpoint assessment window is limited to week 12, which may miss later treatment effects",
      "quote": "Change from baseline (cycle 1 day 1) over time to week 12 in disease related symptoms (dyspnea, cough, and chest pain), physical functioning, and health related quality of life (QOL).",
      "page": 38,
      "section": "2.1.3 Key Secondary Endpoints",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The PRO assessment is truncated at week 12, but PFS and OS endpoints will be followed much longer. This may not capture the full treatment effect on symptoms and QOL, especially if patients remain on treatment beyond 12 weeks, and could underrepresent the benefit of AMG 510.",
      "fix": "Consider extending PRO assessments to a later time point (e.g., week 24 or until progression) to better align with the expected treatment duration."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inclusion criterion 104 requires central confirmation of KRAS p.G12C mutation, which may delay enrollment",
      "quote": "Have documentation of KRAS p.G12C mutation confirmed by central testing through the current protocol or have documentation of KRAS p.G12C mutation through Amgen Study 20190294 prior to enrollment.",
      "page": 58,
      "section": "5.1 Inclusion Criteria",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Requiring central testing for all subjects, unless they were previously tested in another Amgen study, could delay enrollment and add logistical burden. Local testing may be acceptable if validated, and the protocol should allow for that to expedite screening.",
      "fix": "Allow local laboratory confirmation of KRAS p.G12C mutation with central testing for a subset or for confirmation, to reduce screening time."
    },
    {
      "title": "Safety monitoring does not explicitly mention monitoring for interstitial lung disease (ILD), a known class effect for some targeted therapies",
      "quote": "Subject incidence of treatment-emergent adverse events, treatment-related adverse events, changes in vital signs, and clinical laboratory tests.",
      "page": 48,
      "section": "3 Objectives and Endpoints",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The safety endpoint description is generic and does not include specific monitoring for ILD or pneumonitis, which are important for NSCLC patients and may be relevant for KRAS inhibitors. The protocol should include a plan for monitoring and managing ILD to ensure patient safety.",
      "fix": "Add a specific safety monitoring plan for ILD/pneumonitis, including baseline assessment and serial monitoring, and define management guidelines."
    },
    {
      "title": "Primary estimand for PFS censors at start of new anti-cancer therapy, which may introduce bias if treatment switching is common",
      "quote": "PFS is censored at the date of last evaluable assessment before or on start of new anti-cancer therapy.",
      "page": 48,
      "section": "3 Objectives and Endpoints",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Censoring at start of new therapy is a common strategy, but if many patients in the control arm switch to AMG 510 or other therapies, this could lead to informative censoring and bias the PFS estimate. The protocol should consider sensitivity analyses using alternative strategies, such as treatment policy.",
      "fix": "Include sensitivity analyses for PFS that do not censor at start of new therapy, to assess the robustness of the primary estimand."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inclusion criterion 105a: Adjuvant therapy counting as a line is ambiguous for patients who progress after 6 months",
      "quote": "Adjuvant therapy will count as a line of therapy if the subject progressed on or within 6 months of adjuvant therapy administration.",
      "page": 58,
      "section": "5.1 Inclusion Criteria",
      "category": "amendment_risk",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The criterion is clear for progression within 6 months, but it is ambiguous whether adjuvant therapy counts if the subject progresses after 6 months but then receives another line of therapy. This could lead to inconsistent interpretation and potential amendments.",
      "fix": "Clarify that adjuvant therapy counts as a line only if progression occurs within 6 months, and that subsequent lines are counted separately."
    },
    {
      "title": "PRO estimand uses 'change from baseline to Week 12' but does not specify how missing data will be handled",
      "quote": "Change from baseline to Week 12 in PRO endpoints between AMG 510 and docetaxel, for subjects with previously treated locally advanced and unresectable or metastatic NSCLC with KRAS p.G12C mutation.",
      "page": 48,
      "section": "3 Objectives and Endpoints",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The estimand does not describe the handling of missing PRO data, which is common in oncology trials due to disease progression or dropout. Without a clear strategy, the analysis may be biased, and the protocol should specify a method such as mixed models for repeated measures or multiple imputation.",
      "fix": "Add a description of the missing data handling strategy for PRO endpoints in the estimand or statistical analysis section."
    }
  ]
}
